title: Pixel title screen as a road-station woodblock print: bokashi sky, an out-of-register peak, a vertical vermilion title cartouche, stepped menu panels
use: The title screen of a pixel-art game drawn on a 480 x 270 grid and scaled by a whole number (x4 = 1080p). The scene is the style's procedural print; replace it by editing the scene, not by pasting a raster.

selected.note: selected entry (vermilion seal cursor, pale bar)

mist.note: horizontal mist bands across the peak

traveller.note: one 6 px traveller on the road: the scale of the print

logo.note: vertical, 24 px native, on the vermilion cartouche

series.note: vertical, 12 px native, on the paper cartouche

menu_tag.note: beside the selected entry, in the plate red

logo_latin.default: C H A L K R O A D

relations: Title cartouche vertical and vermilion, upper right, its series cartouche in paper beside it; both with the dark-red plate 2 px off.
Menu panels step down and right 12 px per entry, like a road climbing the print.
A dark ink bar at the bottom carries version and copyright: nothing small sits on the dithered field.
decoration: Bokashi sky in dither bands, stars, moon, peak with snow dither and the ink line 1 px off, mist bands, hills, field dither, the paper road, six pines, the station, the traveller: all drawn on the grid.

provenance.corpus: pixel-rpg-ui case round 2 (白垩驿路 CHALKROAD): our own original fictional pixel RPG in the woodblock-pixel grammar
provenance.experiment: styles/woodblock-pixel/style.json provenance; case renders in docs/cases/pixel-rpg-ui
provenance.method: Ported from the case's screens.cjs (scene() and the title UI), drawn on the native grid in code: pixel writes are run-length paths per colour, large dithers are 4 x 4 Bayer patterns; text in the pixel font at 12 / 24 px on whole pixels.
measured: Round 2: first pass 11 contrast findings over the screens (small text on the dithered field 2.48:1, vermilion on the selected bar 4.07:1); final 0, minimum 4.76:1 after the ink bar and dark accents.
Pixel discipline (case snap.py): 0 off-palette pixels before snapping, 0 mixed 4 x 4 blocks at x4, 15 of 16 colours used.
